_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-19 07:42:26Z)**_

The root cause: you're on a headless/SSH session on the Pi. `xclip` is installed but there's no X display (`DISPLAY` unset), so it fails. Same for Wayland (no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`).

The best fix for SSH sessions is **OSC 52** — a terminal escape sequence that ships clipboard data to your local terminal (Ghostty, tmux with `set-clipboard on`, Alacritty, Kitty all support it). Works over SSH with no X/Wayland needed.

Three options:

1. **Add OSC 52 fallback to `x copy`** (recommended) — when no pbcopy/wl-copy works and no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, emit an OSC 52 sequence to `/dev/tty`. Your tmux config already has `set-clipboard on`, so it'll propagate through.

2. **Quick one-off**: run with a display if you have one forwarded (`ssh -X`), or install `wl-clipboard` if the Pi runs Wayland.

3. **For the `sms` case specifically**: make clipboard-copy best-effort (don't fail the command if no backend works).

Want me to implement option 1? It'd update `bin/executable_x` (or wherever the source lives in chezmoi) to try OSC 52 before giving up.
